newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma party holds small gathering at Suu Kyi home.
newsitem.headline: Burma party holds small gathering at Suu Kyi home.

text.p: A small group of opposition leaders met at the home of National League for Democracy (NLD) party leader Aung San Suu Kyi on Tuesday after the military government refused to permit a larger gathering.

A senior opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) source told Reuters by telephone from Suu Kyi's home that only 10 party executive committee members had been allowed into Suu Kyi's house for a meeting.

The NLD had planned to hold a gathering of several hundred party members and elected parliamentarians at Suu Kyi's lakeside rsidence to mark the anniversary of its landslide 1990 election victory, which was not recognised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).

But a government spokesman said: "The NLD has not sought permission to hold such a large gathering. If they hold such a meeting at Suu Kyi's house, they will be stopped. Only the party's executive committee members, family members and those living there can go in." The NLD source said the SLORC had from last week detained up to 316 party members, including about 50 members of parliament, nationwide to thwart the planned special gathering.
The SLORC has denied the charge and asked the NLD to prove the detentions.
Witnesses said that security had been tightened near Suu Kyi's University Avenue residence and stringent checks were made on those intending to visit her home.

Soldiers and riot police were on standby near her home and some NLD members were stopped from entering Suu Kyi's house. Security personnel were also stationed near the home of another senior party leader U Tin Oo.

The NLD source said that most discussions for the planned party's seventh anniversary of its election victory had already been completed on May 26 by those party members who managed to meet in Rangoon.

"Technically, the meeting on the occasion of the seventh anniversary was completed successfully and we will continue with our struggle for democracy until we reach the goal even though the SLORC tries all means to stop us," the source said.
He added that a total of up to 500 party members had gathered in different groups last week to discuss party reports on the economy, political situation justice and other matters.
Analysts said the latest development was expected and represented a face-saving measure for both sides. They said it avoided an ugly standoff and confrontation between the two sides.
The government spokesman agreed that the special NLD meeting held last week had completed its business.
"But although the special meeting has taken place, the NLD will try to stage a meeting on May 27 or 28 at either Suu Kyi's home or other locations," he said.
